sanskrit: ud budhyadhvaṁ samanasaḥ sakhāyaḥ sam agnim indhvam bahavaḥ sanīḻāḥ | dadhikrām agnim uṣasaṁ ca devīm indrāvato 'vase ni hvaye vaḥ ||
english: Awake, O companions of one mind; kindle Agni together, ye many who are gathered as one. I invoke for your protection Dadhikrā, Agni, and the divine Dawn, and the Indra-aided ones.

sanskrit: mandrā kṛṇudhvaṁ dhiya ā tanudhvaṁ nāvam aritraparaṇīṁ kṛṇudhvam | iṣkṛṇudhvam āyudhāraṁ kṛṇudhvam prāñcaṁ yajñam pra ṇayatā sakhāyaḥ ||
english: Make your thoughts glad; stretch out the oar-propelled ship that crosses over; fit the quiver, make ready the weapons; lead forward the sacrifice eastward, O companions.

sanskrit: yunakta sīrā vi yugā tanudhvaṁ kṛte yonau vapateha bījam | girā ca śruṣṭiḥ sabharā asan no nedīya it sṛṇyaḥ pakvam eyāt ||
english: Yoke the ploughs, spread out the yokes; sow the seed here in the prepared womb. May our hymn and the hearing be fruitful; may the sickle come to the ripened grain all the sooner.

sanskrit: sīrā yuñjanti kavayo yugā vi tanvate pṛthak | dhīrā deveṣu sumnayā ||
english: The wise yoke the ploughs and spread the yokes apart one by one; the steadfast ones are gracious toward the gods.

sanskrit: nir āhāvān kṛṇotana saṁ varatrā dadhātana | siñcāmahā avatam udriṇaṁ vayaṁ suṣekam anupakṣitam ||
english: Make the ladles ready; bind the harness-straps together; we will pour into the water-trough that is full, that pours well, inexhaustible.

sanskrit: iṣkṛtāhāvam avataṁ suvaratraṁ suṣecanam | udriṇaṁ siñce akṣitam ||
english: The trough prepared with ladles, having a good harness-strap, pouring well—I pour into the water-filled, inexhaustible.

sanskrit: prīṇītāśvān hitaṁ jayātha svastivāhaṁ ratham it kṛṇudhvam | droṇāhāvam avatam aśmacakram aṁsatrakośaṁ siñcatā nṛpāṇam ||
english: Delight the horses; conquer the well-placed prize; make the chariot that bears good fortune. Pour into the wooden-ladle trough, the stone-wheeled, the shoulder-strap-quiver one—the guardian of men.

sanskrit: vrajaṁ kṛṇudhvaṁ sa hi vo nṛpāṇo varma sīvyadhvam bahulā pṛthūni | puraḥ kṛṇudhvam āyasīr adhṛṣṭā mā vaḥ susroc camaso dṛṁhatā tam ||
english: Build the cattle-pen, for it is your guardian; stitch together armour, broad and wide; build iron, invincible fortresses before you; let not the cup overflow—make it firm.

sanskrit: ā vo dhiyaṁ yajñiyāṁ varta ūtaye devā devīṁ yajatāṁ yajñiyām iha | sā no duhīyad yavaseva gatvī sahasradhārā payasā mahī gauḥ ||
english: Turn your sacred thought toward protection; let the gods here worship the divine, sacrifice-worthy one. May she who goes to the pasture like a cow yield to us with a thousand streams the milk of the great cow.

sanskrit: ā tū ṣiñca harim īṁ dror upasthe vāśībhis takṣatāśmanmayībhiḥ | pari ṣvajadhvaṁ daśa kakṣyābhir ubhe dhurau prati vahniṁ yunakta ||
english: Now pour in the Soma here in the lap of the wooden door; let the stone tools shape it; embrace it with ten girths; yoke the carrier to both shafts.

sanskrit: ubhe dhurau vahnir āpibdamāno 'ntar yoneva carati dvijāniḥ | vanaspatiṁ vana āsthāpayadhvaṁ ni ṣū dadhidhvam akhananta utsam ||
english: The carrier, pressing hard upon both shafts, moves within them like one born of two mothers. Erect the tree of the forest in the forest; dig and set the spring.

sanskrit: kapṛn naraḥ kapṛtham ud dadhātana codayata khudata vājasātaye | niṣṭigryaḥ putram ā cyāvayotaya indraṁ sabādha iha somapītaye ||
english: O men, lift up the phallus, the foremost one; urge it forward, dig for the winning of the prize. Shaking the son from the womb, bring Indra here with pressure to drink the Soma.

sanskrit: pra te ratham mithūkṛtam indro 'vatu dhṛṣṇuyā | asminn ājau puruhūta śravāyye dhanabhakṣeṣu no 'va ||
english: May Indra boldly protect your chariot that is well-paired; O much-invoked one, protect us in this contest worthy of fame, in the seizure of prizes.

sanskrit: ut sma vāto vahati vāso 'syā adhirathaṁ yad ajayat sahasram | rathīr abhūn mudgalānī gaviṣṭau bhare kṛtaṁ vy aced indrasenā ||
english: The wind blows up the garment of this woman who won a thousand from the chariot. Mudgalānī became the charioteer in the cow-race; Indrasenā divided the prize won in the battle.

sanskrit: antar yaccha jighāṁsato vajram indrābhidāsataḥ | dāsasya vā maghavann āryasya vā sanutar yavayā vadham ||
english: Hold back the bolt, O Indra, within your grasp against those who wish to slay, against those who attack; O bounteous one, drive far away the blow of the Dāsa or the Ārya.

sanskrit: udno hradam apibaj jarhṛṣāṇaḥ kūṭaṁ sma tṛṁhad abhimātim eti | pra muṣkabhāraḥ śrava icchamāno 'jiram bāhū abharat siṣāsan ||
english: Exultingly he drank the pond of water; shaking he strikes the peak and goes against the foe; the scrotal-load-bearer, seeking renown, stretching out his arms quick to the field, striving.

sanskrit: ny akrandayann upayanta enam amehayan vṛṣabham madhya ājeḥ | tena sūbharvaṁ śatavat sahasraṁ gavām mudgalaḥ pradhane jigāya ||
english: Lowing, they came up to him; they made the bull urinate in the midst of the race. With him Mudgala won in the final contest a hundredfold, a thousandfold of cattle.

sanskrit: kakardave vṛṣabho yukta āsīd avāvacīt sārathir asya keśī | dudher yuktasya dravataḥ sahānasa ṛcchanti ṣmā niṣpado mudgalānīm ||
english: The bull was yoked to the Kakardave; his charioteer, the long-haired Keśī, drove it. The blows of the running bull dragging the cart fall upon Mudgalānī as she sits.

sanskrit: uta pradhim ud ahann asya vidvān upāyunag vaṁsagam atra śikṣan | indra ud āvat patim aghnyānām araṁhata padyābhiḥ kakudmān ||
english: Knowing it, he knocked out the wheel-felly and here he helped, joining the shaft-piece, seeking to aid. Indra lifted up the lord of the unslayable cows; the hump-necked bull hastened with swift feet.

sanskrit: śunam aṣṭrāvy acarat kapardī varatrāyāṁ dārv ānahyamānaḥ | nṛmṇāni kṛṇvan bahave janāya gāḥ paspaśānas taviṣīr adhatta ||
english: The braided-haired one moved prosperously through the goad; the wood was being fastened to the strap. Performing manly deeds for the many people, watching over the cows, he acquired strengths.

sanskrit: imaṁ tam paśya vṛṣabhasya yuñjaṁ kāṣṭhāyā madhye drughaṇaṁ śayānam | yena jigāya śatavat sahasraṁ gavām mudgalaḥ pṛtanājyeṣu ||
english: See this yoke-fellow of the bull lying in the middle of the course, the wooden block; by means of him Mudgala won a hundredfold, a thousandfold of cattle in the battles.

sanskrit: āre aghā ko nv itthā dadarśa yaṁ yuñjanti tam v ā sthāpayanti | nāsmai tṛṇaṁ nodakam ā bharanty uttaro dhuro vahati pradediśat ||
english: Far away the sins—who ever saw it happen thus? They yoke him and then unharness him too. They bring him neither grass nor water; yet the superior one draws the shaft time and again, as one pointing the way.

sanskrit: parivṛkteva patividyam ānaṭ pīpyānā kūcakreṇeva siñcan | eṣaiṣyā cid rathyā jayema sumaṅgalaṁ sinavad astu sātam ||
english: Like an abandoned wife she understood her husband; swelling, pouring like water from a bent wheel. In this very racing-chariot let us conquer; let the winning be auspicious and lucky.

sanskrit: tvaṁ viśvasya jagataś cakṣur indrāsi cakṣuṣaḥ | vṛṣā yad ājiṁ vṛṣaṇā siṣāsasi codayan vadhriṇā yujā ||
english: You, O Indra, are the eye of all the world, the eye among eyes. You are the bull; you urge on the bull-pair to seize the race, goading them with the castrated one as yokefellow.

sanskrit: āśuḥ śiśāno vṛṣabho na bhīmo ghanāghanaḥ kṣobhaṇaś carṣaṇīnām | saṁkrandano 'nimiṣa ekavīraḥ śataṁ senā ajayat sākam indraḥ ||
english: Swift, whetted, terrible like a bull, striker upon striker, shaker of peoples, the battle-shouter, ever-wakeful, sole hero—Indra conquered a hundred armies together.

sanskrit: saṁkrandanenānimiṣeṇa jiṣṇunā yutkāreṇa duścyavanena dhṛṣṇunā | tad indreṇa jayata tat sahadhvaṁ yudho nara iṣuhastena vṛṣṇā ||
english: Conquer with him, the battle-shouter, the unwinking, the victorious, the battle-crying, the hard-to-shake, the bold one; withstand that with Indra, O men—with the arrow-holding bull.

sanskrit: sa iṣuhastaiḥ sa niṣaṅgibhir vaśī saṁsraṣṭā sa yudha indro gaṇeṇa | saṁsṛṣṭajit somapā bāhuśardhy ugradhanvā pratihitābhir astā ||
english: He with arrow-bearers, he with quiver-wearers is master, joined in battle with Indra and his troop. The conqueror in close combat, the Soma-drinker, mighty in arms, with terrible bow, shooting with arrows fitted to the string.

sanskrit: bṛhaspate pari dīyā rathena rakṣohāmitrān apabādhamānaḥ | prabhañjan senāḥ pramṛṇo yudhā jayann asmākam edhy avitā rathānām ||
english: O Bṛhaspati, drive around with your chariot, driving away the Rākṣasas and enemies; breaking armies, crushing in battle, conquering—be the protector of our chariots.

sanskrit: balavijñāyaḥ sthaviraḥ pravīraḥ sahasvān vājī sahamāna ugraḥ | abhivīro abhisatvā sahojā jaitram indra ratham ā tiṣṭha govit ||
english: Known by his strength, firm, pre-eminent in heroism, powerful, strong, enduring, terrible; mighty over heroes, bold in battle, born of power—mount the victorious chariot, O Indra, finder of cows.

sanskrit: gotrabhidaṁ govidaṁ vajrabāhuṁ jayantam ajma pramṛṇantam ojasā | imaṁ sajātā anu vīrayadhvam indraṁ sakhāyo anu saṁ rabhadhvam ||
english: The breaker of cow-pens, the finder of cows, the thunderbolt-armed, conquering in the course, crushing with might—let the kinsmen follow him in heroism; embrace Indra closely, O companions.

sanskrit: abhi gotrāṇi sahasā gāhamāno 'dayo vīraḥ śatamanyur indraḥ | duścyavanaḥ pṛtanāṣāḻ ayudhyo 'smākaṁ senā avatu pra yutsu ||
english: Plunging mightily into the cow-pens, unhurt, the hero of hundredfold wrath—Indra, hard to shake, conqueror of armies, not to be defeated in battle—let him protect our army in the combat.

sanskrit: indra āsāṁ netā bṛhaspatir dakṣiṇā yajñaḥ pura etu somaḥ | devasenānām abhibhañjatīnāṁ jayantīnām maruto yantv agram ||
english: Let Indra be the leader of these, Bṛhaspati on the right, the sacrifice advance, Soma in front; let the Maruts go at the head of the divine armies that overwhelm and conquer.

sanskrit: indrasya vṛṣṇo varuṇasya rājña ādityānām marutāṁ śardha ugram | mahāmanasām bhuvanacyavānāṁ ghoṣo devānāṁ jayatām ud asthāt ||
english: The war-cry of Indra the bull, of Varuṇa the king, of the Ādityas, of the terrible host of Maruts—of the great-spirited, world-shaking, conquering gods—has arisen.

sanskrit: ud dharṣaya maghavann āyudhāny ut satvanām māmakānām manāṁsi | ud vṛtrahan vājināṁ vājināny ud rathānāṁ jayatāṁ yantu ghoṣāḥ ||
english: Exhilarate the weapons, O bounteous one; exhilarate the spirits of my warriors; let the strengths of the prize-winners rise up, O Vṛtra-slayer; let the war-cries of the conquering chariots go forth.

sanskrit: asmākam indraḥ samṛteṣu dhvajeṣv asmākaṁ yā iṣavas tā jayantu | asmākaṁ vīrā uttare bhavantv asmāṁ u devā avatā haveṣu ||
english: May Indra be with our banners in the encounters; let those arrows of ours conquer; may our heroes be supreme; and do you, O gods, protect us in our calls.

sanskrit: amīṣāṁ cittam pratilobhayantī gṛhāṇāṅgāny apve parehi | abhi prehi nir daha hṛtsu śokair andhenāmitrās tamasā sacantām ||
english: Beguiling the minds of those enemies, seize their limbs, O Apvā, and pass through; advance upon them, burn them with pain in their hearts; let the foes be joined by the blinding darkness.

sanskrit: pretā jayatā nara indro vaḥ śarma yacchatu | ugrā vaḥ santu bāhavo 'nādhṛṣyā yathāsatha ||
english: Go forward, O men, conquer; may Indra grant you shelter. May your arms be terrible and irresistible, as indeed you are.

sanskrit: asāvi somaḥ puruhūta tubhyaṁ haribhyāṁ yajñam upa yāhi tūyam | tubhyaṁ giro vipravīrā iyānā dadhanvira indra pibā sutasya ||
english: The Soma has been pressed for you, O much-invoked Indra; come quickly with your two bay horses to the sacrifice. For you the songs of the inspired heroes speed forward; O unconquerable Indra, drink of the pressed juice.

sanskrit: apsu dhūtasya harivaḥ pibeha nṛbhiḥ sutasya jaṭharam pṛṇasva | mimikṣur yam adraya indra tubhyaṁ tebhir vardhasva madam ukthavāhaḥ ||
english: Drink here of what has been purified in the waters, O bay-horsed one; fill your belly with what is pressed by men. The stones have mixed it for you, O Indra; grow strong on them, you who carry the hymn.

sanskrit: progrām pītiṁ vṛṣṇa iyarmi satyām prayai sutasya haryaśva tubhyam | indra dhenābhir iha mādayasva dhībhir viśvābhiḥ śacyā gṛṇānaḥ ||
english: I urge you, O bull, to the true foremost drinking—for the outpouring of the pressed juice for you, O bay-horsed one. Delight yourself here, O Indra, with the melodies, with all thoughts, being praised by your might.

sanskrit: ūtī śacīvas tava vīryeṇa vayo dadhānā uśija ṛtajñāḥ | prajāvad indra manuṣo duroṇe tasthur gṛṇantaḥ sadhamādyāsaḥ ||
english: With your protection, O lord of might, laying hold of strength by your valour—the eager ones, knowers of the sacred order—they stood exulting in the house of Manu, praising you with progeny, O Indra.

sanskrit: praṇītibhiṣ ṭe haryaśva suṣṭoḥ suṣumnasya pururuco janāsaḥ | maṁhiṣṭhām ūtiṁ vitire dadhānāḥ stotāra indra tava sūnṛtābhiḥ ||
english: By your leaderships, O bay-horsed one, of you the well-praised, the benevolent, the widely shining—the peoples, holding on to the most bounteous help, spread out as your praisers, O Indra, with your true words.

sanskrit: upa brahmāṇi harivo haribhyāṁ somasya yāhi pītaye sutasya | indra tvā yajñaḥ kṣamamāṇam ānaḍ dāśvāṁ asy adhvarasya praketaḥ ||
english: Come with your two bay horses to the prayers, O bay-horsed one, to drink of the pressed Soma. O Indra, the sacrifice has found you patient; you are the foremost knower of the oblation.

sanskrit: sahasravājam abhimātiṣāhaṁ suteraṇam maghavānaṁ suvṛktim | upa bhūṣanti giro apratītam indraṁ namasyā jarituḥ pananta ||
english: Songs adorn the one of a thousand prizes, the overpowerer of aggressors, the good leader, the bounteous, the well-hymned—the unconquered Indra; they marvel at him with reverence, the singers.

sanskrit: saptāpo devīḥ suraṇā amṛktā yābhiḥ sindhum atara indra pūrbhit | navatiṁ srotyā nava ca sravantīr devebhyo gātum manuṣe ca vindaḥ ||
english: The seven divine waters, clear, unblended—with which you crossed the river, O Indra, fort-breaker—ninety streams and nine more flowing: you found the path for gods and for man.

sanskrit: apo mahīr abhiśaster amuñco 'jāgar āsv adhi deva ekaḥ | indra yās tvaṁ vṛtratūrye cakartha tābhir viśvāyus tanvam pupuṣyāḥ ||
english: You freed the great waters from the curse; the one god was awake over them. O Indra, with those waters with which you performed the conquest of Vṛtra, may you nourish your body, giving universal life.

sanskrit: vīreṇyaḥ kratur indraḥ suśastir utāpi dhenā puruhūtam īṭṭe | ārdayad vṛtram akṛṇod u lokaṁ sasāhe śakraḥ pṛtanā abhiṣṭiḥ ||
english: Indra the heroic, the resolve, the well-proclaimed—and the melody seeks the much-invoked one. He shattered Vṛtra and made space; the Mighty One, the vanquisher, has overcome the armies.

sanskrit: śunaṁ huvema maghavānam indram asmin bhare nṛtamaṁ vājasātau | śṛṇvantam ugram ūtaye samatsu ghnantaṁ vṛtrāṇi saṁjitaṁ dhanānām ||
english: We call for our welfare the bounteous Indra, the most manly in this battle at the winning of the prize—the one who listens, the terrible, for our protection in combats, the slayer of Vṛtras, the gatherer of riches.

sanskrit: kadā vaso stotraṁ haryata āva śmaśā rudhad vāḥ | dīrghaṁ sutaṁ vātāpyāya ||
english: When, O good lord, will the praise you love come to you? The blade will stop—for the long-pressed Soma waiting for the wind to dry it.

sanskrit: harī yasya suyujā vivratā ver arvantānu śepā | ubhā rajī na keśinā patir dan ||
english: He whose two bay horses are well-yoked, going different ways like birds, following their impulse according to their tails—both long-maned like coursers—the lord has given.

sanskrit: apa yor indraḥ pāpaja ā marto na śaśramāṇo bibhīvān | śubhe yad yuyuje taviṣīvān ||
english: From the two Indra removes evil; no mortal who has exerted himself is afraid—when the mighty one has yoked for beauty.

sanskrit: sacāyor indraś carkṛṣa āṁ upānasaḥ saparyan | nadayor vivratayoḥ śūra indraḥ ||
english: Together with the two, Indra ploughed and ploughed again—of two carts serving together—of two streams going separate ways: the hero, Indra.

sanskrit: adhi yas tasthau keśavantā vyacasvantā na puṣṭyai | vanoti śiprābhyāṁ śipriṇīvān ||
english: He who stood upon the two long-maned ones, wide-stretching, not for nourishment—he wins with his cheek-pieces, like one with strong cheeks.

sanskrit: prāstaud ṛṣvaujā ṛṣvebhis tatakṣa śūraḥ śavasā | ṛbhur na kratubhir mātariśvā ||
english: He of lofty strength proclaimed; the hero fashioned with lofty ones by might—like Ṛbhu in designs, like Mātariśvan.

sanskrit: vajraṁ yaś cakre suhanāya dasyave hirīmaśo hirīmān | arutahanur adbhutaṁ na rajaḥ ||
english: He who made the thunderbolt for the good smiting of the Dasyu—the golden-maned one, with golden mane—of unwounded jaw, wondrous as the bright space.

sanskrit: ava no vṛjinā śiśīhy ṛcā vanemānṛcaḥ | nābrahmā yajña ṛdhag joṣati tve ||
english: Sharpen away our sins with the hymn; we who sing hymns would beat down the unsinging. No non-Brahman, no sacrifice thrives separately from you.

sanskrit: ūrdhvā yat te tretinī bhūd yajñasya dhūrṣu sadman | sajūr nāvaṁ svayaśasaṁ sacāyoḥ ||
english: When your triple fire stood erect in the dwellings at the shafts of the sacrifice—in unison with the self-glorious ship of the two companions.

sanskrit: śriye te pṛśnir upasecanī bhūc chriye darvir arepāḥ | yayā sve pātre siñcasa ut ||
english: May the dappled one be for your glory an over-pourer; may the spotless ladle be for your glory—with which you pour upward into your own cup.

sanskrit: śataṁ vā yad asurya prati tvā sumitra itthāstaud durmitra itthāstaut | āvo yad dasyuhatye kutsaputram prāvo yad dasyuhatye kutsavatsam ||
english: Whether it was a hundred, O lordly one, that Sumitra praised you thus or that Durmitra praised you thus—when you helped in the slaying of Dasyus the son of Kutsa, when you helped in the slaying of Dasyus the calf of Kutsa.

sanskrit: ubhā u nūnaṁ tad id arthayethe vi tanvāthe dhiyo vastrāpaseva | sadhrīcīnā yātave prem ajīgaḥ sudineva pṛkṣa ā taṁsayethe ||
english: Both of you now seek that very thing; you spread your thoughts like weavers at their work. Going forth together you have started us onward; like refreshment on a fair day you weave us close.

sanskrit: uṣṭāreva pharvareṣu śrayethe prāyogeva śvātryā śāsur ethaḥ | dūteva hi ṣṭho yaśasā janeṣu māpa sthātam mahiṣevāvapānāt ||
english: You rest like camels among the horses; you go like a swift course over the instructed. For you are like messengers of renown among the peoples; do not stay away from us like a buffalo from the drinking-place.

sanskrit: sākaṁyujā śakunasyeva pakṣā paśveva citrā yajur ā gamiṣṭam | agnir iva devayor dīdivāṁsā parijmāneva yajathaḥ purutrā ||
english: Come together yoked, like the two wings of a bird, like wonderfully varied beasts with the oblation. Blazing like fire for the two divine ones, ranging about, you two worship in many places.

sanskrit: āpī vo asme pitareva putro greva rucā nṛpatīva turyai | iryeva puṣṭyai kiraṇeva bhujyai śruṣṭīvāneva havam ā gamiṣṭam ||
english: Be our intimate friend—like a father to a son, like a great one with splendour for swiftness, like wind for nourishment, like a ray for enjoyment—come to our call, as one eager to listen.

sanskrit: vaṁsageva pūṣaryā śimbātā mitreva ṛtā śatarā śātapantā | vājevoccā vayasā gharmyeṣṭhā meṣeveṣā saparyā purīṣā ||
english: Like the shaft-joint of the Pūṣan-chariot, pair of pods; like Mitra in truth, hundred-rayed, a hundred-winged; dwelling aloft with strength at a prize like the Gharma-fire; worshipping like a ram, seeking fulfillment.

sanskrit: sṛṇyeva jarbharī turpharītū naitośeva turpharī parpharīkā | udanyajeva jemanā maderū tā me jarāyv ajaram marāyu ||
english: Swiftly moving like a sickle, swift-going pair; swift-going, flickering like a naitośa creeper; conquering like water-born ones, the two exhilarating ones—those two, Jarāyu and the undecaying Marāyu, for me.

sanskrit: pajreva carcaraṁ jāram marāyu kṣadmevārtheṣu tartarītha ugrā | ṛbhū nāpat kharamajrā kharajrur vāyur na parpharat kṣayad rayīṇām ||
english: Like the Pajras, the love-lorn Marāyu goes round and round; fierce like a sharp blade you two traverse the transactions. Like the offspring of the Ṛbhus, swift-striding of rough gait, fluttering like the wind, ruling over riches.

sanskrit: gharmeva madhu jaṭhare sanerū bhagevitā turpharī phārivāram | patareva cacarā candranirṇiṅ manaṛṅgā mananyā na jagmī ||
english: Like the Gharma-vessel with honey in the belly, the two old ones—the swift-going Bhagavitā pours abundantly; wandering like birds with silvery adornment, mind-adorned, mind-going, not going hither.

sanskrit: bṛhanteva gambhareṣu pratiṣṭhām pādeva gādhaṁ tarate vidāthaḥ | karṇeva śāsur anu hi smarātho 'ṁśeva no bhajataṁ citram apnaḥ ||
english: Like tall ones you find footing in deep places; like a foot you cross the ford in the assembly. Like an ear you remember the instruction—yes; give us bright wealth, like a portion.

sanskrit: āraṅgareva madhv erayethe sāragheva gavi nīcīnabāre | kīnāreva svedam āsiṣvidānā kṣāmevorjā sūyavasāt sacethe ||
english: You two send forth honey like the Āraṅgara plant; like a bee in the cow downward-armed; dripping with sweat like a kīnāra worm, you two follow with strength from the good grass-land, as from an arid soil.

sanskrit: ṛdhyāma stomaṁ sanuyāma vājam ā no mantraṁ sarathehopa yātam | yaśo na pakvam madhu goṣv antar ā bhūtāṁśo aśvinoḥ kāmam aprāḥ ||
english: May we succeed with our hymn of praise, may we win the prize; come to our chant here together on the chariot. Like fame, like ripe honey among the cows—fulfil the desire of the Aśvins, O share of what comes to be.

sanskrit: āvir abhūn mahi māghonam eṣāṁ viśvaṁ jīvaṁ tamaso nir amoci | mahi jyotiḥ pitṛbhir dattam āgād uruḥ panthā dakṣiṇāyā adarśi ||
english: Great generosity of these patrons became manifest; all living things were released from darkness. The great light given by the fathers has come; the broad path of the Dakṣiṇā has been seen.

sanskrit: uccā divi dakṣiṇāvanto asthur ye aśvadāḥ saha te sūryeṇa | hiraṇyadā amṛtatvam bhajante vāsodāḥ soma pra tiranta āyuḥ ||
english: The givers of the Dakṣiṇā stood high in heaven; those who gave horses—they stood with the sun. The givers of gold partake of immortality; the givers of garments, O Soma, extend their life.

sanskrit: daivī pūrtir dakṣiṇā devayajyā na kavāribhyo nahi te pṛṇanti | athā naraḥ prayatadakṣiṇāso 'vadyabhiyā bahavaḥ pṛṇanti ||
english: The divine fulfilment, the Dakṣiṇā of the god-worship, belongs not to the greedy—for they do not give. But then the men of stretched-forth Dakṣiṇā, fearing blame, the many give.

sanskrit: śatadhāraṁ vāyum arkaṁ svarvidaṁ nṛcakṣasas te abhi cakṣate haviḥ | ye pṛṇanti pra ca yacchanti saṁgame te dakṣiṇāṁ duhate saptamātaram ||
english: Those who see men look upon the hundred-streamed wind, the hymn, the finder of heaven, as an oblation. Those who give and bestow at the assembly—they milk the Dakṣiṇā with its seven mothers.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇāvān prathamo hūta eti dakṣiṇāvān grāmaṇīr agram eti | tam eva manye nṛpatiṁ janānāṁ yaḥ prathamo dakṣiṇām āvivāya ||
english: The one who has Dakṣiṇā goes first when invoked; the one with Dakṣiṇā, the village leader, goes in front. Him alone I regard as the king of peoples—who first set the Dakṣiṇā in motion.

sanskrit: tam eva ṛṣiṁ tam u brahmāṇam āhur yajñanyaṁ sāmagām ukthaśāsam | sa śukrasya tanvo veda tisro yaḥ prathamo dakṣiṇayā rarādha ||
english: Him alone they call the Ṛṣi, him the Brahman—the sacrificial Sāma-singer, the reciter of hymns. He knows the three bodies of the Bright One, who first prospered through the Dakṣiṇā.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇāśvaṁ dakṣiṇā gāṁ dadāti dakṣiṇā candram uta yad dhiraṇyam | dakṣiṇānnaṁ vanute yo na ātmā dakṣiṇāṁ varma kṛṇute vijānan ||
english: The Dakṣiṇā gives the horse, the Dakṣiṇā gives the cow; the Dakṣiṇā gives the moon and also gold. He who is the soul wins food through the Dakṣiṇā; the knowing one makes the Dakṣiṇā his armour.

sanskrit: na bhojā mamrur na nyartham īyur na riṣyanti na vyathante ha bhojāḥ | idaṁ yad viśvam bhuvanaṁ svaś caitat sarvaṁ dakṣiṇaibhyo dadāti ||
english: The generous patrons have not died nor gone to lowliness; the generous are not harmed, nor do they waver. This all, whatever this whole world and heaven—all this is given to those who give the Dakṣiṇā.

sanskrit: bhojā jigyuḥ surabhiṁ yonim agre bhojā jigyur vadhvaṁ yā suvāsāḥ | bhojā jigyur antaḥpeyaṁ surāyā bhojā jigyur ye ahūtāḥ prayanti ||
english: The generous won the fragrant womb first; the generous won the bride who is well-dressed. The generous won the inner draught of the Surā; the generous won—those who go without being invited.

sanskrit: bhojāyāśvaṁ sam mṛjanty āśum bhojāyāste kanyā śumbhamānā | bhojasyedam puṣkariṇīva veśma pariṣkṛtaṁ devamāneva citram ||
english: For the generous one they groom the swift horse; for the generous one the maiden adorns herself sitting. The home of the generous is like a lotus pool, adorned, wondrous like one esteemed by the gods.

sanskrit: bhojam aśvāḥ suṣṭhuvāho vahanti suvṛd ratho vartate dakṣiṇāyāḥ | bhojaṁ devāso 'vatā bhareṣu bhojaḥ śatrūn samanīkeṣu jetā ||
english: Horses with well-carrying loads carry the generous one; the well-wheeled chariot of the Dakṣiṇā rolls. The gods protect the generous in battles; the generous one is the conqueror of foes in the clash of armies.

sanskrit: kim icchantī saramā predam ānaḍ dūre hy adhvā jaguriḥ parācaiḥ | kāsmehitiḥ kā paritakmyāsīt kathaṁ rasāyā ataraḥ payāṁsi ||
english: What desiring has Saramā approached to this place? For the path is far, leading away beyond. What was the errand, what the commission? How did you cross the waters of the Rasā?

sanskrit: indrasya dūtīr iṣitā carāmi maha icchantī paṇayo nidhīn vaḥ | atiṣkado bhiyasā tan na āvat tathā rasāyā ataram payāṁsi ||
english: I roam as the sent messenger of Indra, seeking your great treasures, O Paṇis. A swift leap in fear helped us across—thus I crossed the waters of the Rasā.

sanskrit: kīdṛṅṅ indraḥ sarame kā dṛśīkā yasyedaṁ dūtīr asaraḥ parākāt | ā ca gacchān mitram enā dadhāmāthā gavāṁ gopatir no bhavāti ||
english: What is Indra like, O Saramā, what does he look like—as whose messenger you have come from afar? Let him come here; we will make friendship with him; then let him be the lord of our cattle.

sanskrit: nāhaṁ taṁ veda dabhyaṁ dabhat sa yasyedaṁ dūtīr asaram parākāt | na taṁ gūhanti sravato gabhīrā hatā indreṇa paṇayaḥ śayadhve ||
english: I do not know him as one to be deceived—he who would deceive, it will hit him—as whose messenger I came from afar. Deep flowing streams do not hide him; slain by Indra, O Paṇis, you shall lie.

sanskrit: imā gāvaḥ sarame yā aicchaḥ pari divo antān subhage patantī | kas ta enā ava sṛjād ayudhvy utāsmākam āyudhā santi tigmā ||
english: These are the cows, O Saramā, that you were seeking, flying around the ends of heaven, O fortunate one. Who would release these for you without fighting? And our weapons are sharp.

sanskrit: asenyā vaḥ paṇayo vacāṁsy aniṣavyās tanvaḥ santu pāpīḥ | adhṛṣṭo va etavā astu panthā bṛhaspatir va ubhayā na mṛḻāt ||
english: Not fit to be commanded are your words, O Paṇis; your bodies are not fit for arrows—let them be evil. Let the path for you be impassable; may Bṛhaspati not show mercy to you in either way.

sanskrit: ayaṁ nidhiḥ sarame adribudhno gobhir aśvebhir vasubhir nyṛṣṭaḥ | rakṣanti tam paṇayo ye sugopā reku padam alakam ā jagantha ||
english: This treasure, O Saramā, based in the rock, filled with cows, horses, and riches—the Paṇis guard it, those who are good herdsmen; you have come to a vain, empty step, O messenger.

sanskrit: eha gamann ṛṣayaḥ somaśitā ayāsyo aṅgiraso navagvāḥ | ta etam ūrvaṁ vi bhajanta gonām athaitad vacaḥ paṇayo vamann it ||
english: The Ṛṣis shall come here, sharpened by Soma—Ayāsya, the Aṅgirasas, the Navagvas. They will share out this pen of cows—and then, O Paṇis, your words will vomit forth.

sanskrit: evā ca tvaṁ sarama ājagantha prabādhitā sahasā daivyena | svasāraṁ tvā kṛṇavai mā punar gā apa te gavāṁ subhage bhajāma ||
english: So then you have come here, O Saramā, driven by divine force. We will make you our sister; do not go back. We will give you a share of the cows, O fortunate one.

sanskrit: nāhaṁ veda bhrātṛtvaṁ no svasṛtvam indro vidur aṅgirasaś ca ghorāḥ | gokāmā me acchadayan yad āyam apāta ita paṇayo varīyaḥ ||
english: I know no brotherhood nor sisterhood; Indra knows it, and the terrible Aṅgirasas. The desire for cows concealed from me when I came—fly hence, O Paṇis, afar.

sanskrit: dūram ita paṇayo varīya ud gāvo yantu minatīr ṛtena | bṛhaspatir yā avindan nigūḻhāḥ somo grāvāṇa ṛṣayaś ca viprāḥ ||
english: Go far away, O Paṇis—far away! Let the cows go forth, released by the sacred law. The cows that Bṛhaspati found hidden, and Soma, and the pressing stones, and the inspired Ṛṣis.

sanskrit: te 'vadan prathamā brahmakilbiṣe 'kūpāraḥ salilo mātariśvā | vīḻuharās tapa ugro mayobhūr āpo devīḥ prathamajā ṛtena ||
english: These were the first to speak about the Brahman's offence: the Boundless Ocean, the Waters, Mātariśvan, the Remover of the Firm, the fierce Tapas the bliss-giver, the divine Waters firstborn by the sacred law.

sanskrit: somo rājā prathamo brahmajāyām punaḥ prāyacchad ahṛṇīyamānaḥ | anvartitā varuṇo mitra āsīd agnir hotā hastagṛhyā nināya ||
english: Soma the king was the first to restore the Brahman's wife, giving her back without anger. Varuṇa and Mitra were his followers; Agni the hotar led her taking her by the hand.

sanskrit: hastenaiva grāhya ādhir asyā brahmajāyeyam iti ced avocan | na dūtāya prahye tastha eṣā tathā rāṣṭraṁ gupitaṁ kṣatriyasya ||
english: Her pledge should be taken by the hand alone—'this is the Brahman's wife,' so they said. She is not to be sent to a messenger; thus the realm of the Kṣatriya is protected.

sanskrit: devā etasyām avadanta pūrve saptaṛṣayas tapase ye niṣeduḥ | bhīmā jāyā brāhmaṇasyopanītā durdhāṁ dadhāti parame vyoman ||
english: The gods of old spoke about this matter, and the seven Ṛṣis who sat down to austerity: the wife brought home of a Brahman is terrible; she brings an evil condition in the highest heaven.

sanskrit: brahmacārī carati veviṣad viṣaḥ sa devānām bhavaty ekam aṅgam | tena jāyām anv avindad bṛhaspatiḥ somena nītāṁ juhvaṁ na devāḥ ||
english: The Brahma-student wanders, pouring out poison; he becomes a single limb of the gods. By means of him Bṛhaspati found again his wife who had been led away by Soma—like the gods the ladle.

sanskrit: punar vai devā adaduḥ punar manuṣyā uta | rājānaḥ satyaṁ kṛṇvānā brahmajāyām punar daduḥ ||
english: The gods gave her back again; and humans too gave her back. The kings, acting in truth, gave the Brahman's wife back again.

sanskrit: punardāya brahmajāyāṁ kṛtvī devair nikilbiṣam | ūrjam pṛthivyā bhaktvāyorugāyam upāsate ||
english: Having given back the Brahman's wife, having removed the offence together with the gods, they worship the wide-stepping one, having partaken of the nourishment of the earth.

sanskrit: samiddho adya manuṣo duroṇe devo devān yajasi jātavedaḥ | ā ca vaha mitramahaś cikitvān tvaṁ dūtaḥ kavir asi pracetāḥ ||
english: Kindled today in the house of Manu, O Jātavedas, as god you worship the gods. Come and bring them, O friend of Mitra, discerning one; you are the messenger, the sage, the all-knowing.

sanskrit: tanūnapāt patha ṛtasya yānān madhvā samañjan svadayā sujihva | manmāni dhībhir uta yajñam ṛndhan devatrā ca kṛṇuhy adhvaraṁ naḥ ||
english: O Tanūnapāt, anointing with honey those who travel the paths of sacred law, making them sweet, O fair-tongued one—perfecting our thoughts with prayers and the sacrifice—make our oblation reach the gods.

sanskrit: ājuhvāna īḍyo vandyaś cā yāhy agne vasubhiḥ sajoṣāḥ | tvaṁ devānām asi yahva hotā sa enān yakṣīṣito yajīyān ||
english: Being invoked, worthy of praise and worship—come, O Agni, in harmony with the Vasus. You are the youngest Hotar of the gods; being sent, you most fit to sacrifice—worship them.

sanskrit: prācīnam barhiḥ pradiśā pṛthivyā vastor asyā vṛjyate agre ahnām | vy u prathate vitaraṁ varīyo devebhyo aditaye syonam ||
english: The sacred grass is strewn facing east, spread at the point of this abode at the beginning of the days. It spreads out broader and wider, a soft seat for the gods and for Aditi.

sanskrit: vyacasvatīr urviyā vi śrayantām patibhyo na janayaḥ śumbhamānāḥ | devīr dvāro bṛhatīr viśvaminvā devebhyo bhavata suprāyaṇāḥ ||
english: Let the spacious ones spread themselves wide, adorning themselves like wives for their lords. O divine doors, broad and all-filling, be good entrance ways for the gods.

sanskrit: ā suṣvayantī yajate upāke uṣāsānaktā sadatāṁ ni yonau | divye yoṣaṇe bṛhatī surukme adhi śriyaṁ śukrapiśaṁ dadhāne ||
english: The two who flow fair and are worshipped nearby—let Night-and-Dawn sit down in their womb, the two divine maidens, tall and well-adorned, assuming the bright, white-gleaming splendour.

sanskrit: daivyā hotārā prathamā suvācā mimānā yajñam manuṣo yajadhyai | pracodayantā vidatheṣu kārū prācīnaṁ jyotiḥ pradiśā diśantā ||
english: The two divine Hotars, the first, the fair-voiced, measuring out the sacrifice for man to worship—inspiring the two artisans at the assemblies, directing the eastern light according to the quarter.

sanskrit: ā no yajñam bhāratī tūyam etv iḻā manuṣvad iha cetayantī | tisro devīr barhir edaṁ syonaṁ sarasvatī svapasaḥ sadantu ||
english: Let Bhāratī come swiftly to our sacrifice; let Iḷā awaken here in the manner of Manu; let the three goddesses—Sarasvatī, the skilful-working ones—sit on this comfortable sacred grass.

sanskrit: ya ime dyāvāpṛthivī janitrī rūpair apiṁśad bhuvanāni viśvā | tam adya hotar iṣito yajīyān devaṁ tvaṣṭāram iha yakṣi vidvān ||
english: He who fashioned all the worlds with forms—him, these two parents Heaven and Earth—worship here today, O Hotar, sent and most fit to sacrifice, knowing it—the god Tvaṣṭṛ.

sanskrit: upāvasṛja tmanyā samañjan devānām pātha ṛtuthā havīṁṣi | vanaspatiḥ śamitā devo agniḥ svadantu havyam madhunā ghṛtena ||
english: Release of yourself, anointing, setting the oblations in their season upon the path of the gods—let the tree, the slaughterer, and the divine Agni make the offering savoury with honey and ghee.

sanskrit: sadyo jāto vy amimīta yajñam agnir devānām abhavat purogāḥ | asya hotuḥ pradiśy ṛtasya vāci svāhākṛtaṁ havir adantu devāḥ ||
english: Born at once, Agni measured out the sacrifice; he became the forerunner of the gods. In the direction of this Hotar, in the voice of the sacred law, let the gods eat the oblation consecrated with Svāhā.
